- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap peak values.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or lagged mean reversion after peak.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.25 for 3+ days), model frequently overestimates upside — cap forecast growth rate or introduce early mean-reversion bias.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly bearish, model often underestimates downside risk — add small downward bias or adjust for volatility clustering.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate volatility in early/late periods — apply smoothing or adjust for sentiment-driven volatility spikes.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model often fails to anticipate reversal — introduce lagged sentiment reversal heuristics (e.g., if sentiment drops below -0.15, reduce forecast slope by 5–10%).
- Avoid linear extrapolation — model often assumes trend continuation when sentiment shifts — use sentiment-weighted moving average or adaptive decay for trend smoothing.
